reasoning: Analyzing FairTix's automation landscape reveals a ticketing platform with sophisticated anti-bot positioning but critical operational gaps. The company has built AI-powered support automation achieving 94-100% success rates, yet their core revenue workflow (lottery winner notifications) fails 36% of the time. All customer-facing workflows are inactive despite production-ready templates. The most glaring gap: payment processing and ticket delivery - referenced throughout but completely absent from automation. With lottery winners getting 24-hour purchase windows, manual payment handling creates a severe bottleneck. The Fair Queue algorithm that differentiates their business exists only as output in sheets, not as visible automation. Gmail dependency (87.5% of workflows) creates a single point of failure. Three immediate actions emerge: fix the failing lottery notification workflow, build payment automation to capture revenue within 24-hour windows, and consolidate duplicate workflows that create maintenance confusion.

recommendations.reasoning: The lottery winner notification workflow shows 36% failure rate with no retry logic, directly causing revenue loss. This is FairTix's primary revenue driver - winners who don't receive notifications can't purchase within their 24-hour window. The workflow exists, executes regularly, but fails silently. This is a pure technical fix with immediate revenue impact. Evidence is conclusive from execution data.

recommendations.affectedScope: FairTix Lottery Winner Notification System workflow
recommendations.implementationNotes: Enable retry logic on Gmail send node, implement exponential backoff, add success confirmation loop, ensure error workflow is active and notifying team
